MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 6, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:02 p.m., on May 6, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 3, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ury
  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference With Legal Counsel -- Anticipated Litigation. Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: (One
  Case.)

City Council Minutes  1  May 6, 2013
 CS2. Labor Negotiations-The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are
  the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to declare a need to
consider a Closed Session matter (CS3) which arose subsequent to the posting of the Agenda and
to affirm that the matter must be considered before the next meeting with the recommendation
that it be addressed in closed session tonight.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel—Consideration of Commencement of Litigation.
  Subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9 (One Potential Case - Challenge to DOF Claim on
  City Funds.)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:13 p.m., with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council spent the majority of the time considering
the late added agenda item (CS3) regarding potential litigation with the State of California
Department of Finance and related County agencies. The discussion was relative to the State's
demand that the City pay $500,000 by Friday, May 10, 2013. The City has some dispute with
this finding and the Council has authorized the commencement of litigation to try and bring this
matter to a more favorable outcome for the City.

For item CS1, the Council and staff held a general discussion regarding litigation matters and
item CS2 was not considered due to lack of time.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Better Vision for Children Awareness Proclamation

  Mayor Reardon presented the proclamation to Tom Cataldo, Betty Gallup and Jeanne
  Cassidy from the Better Vision for Children Foundation.

P2. Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winners

City Council Minutes  2  May 6, 2013
   Michelle Clark from Waste Management presented the Community Recycling Program
  Award to Legacy Partners and TRR Real Estate.

P3. Presentation of Awards to Deputies Adam Sandler, John Popp, Lee Martinez, and
  Ron Rhodes by Mothers Against Drunk Drivers (MADD).

  Sherry Graham from Mothers Against Drunk Drivers (MADD) and Mayor Reardon
  presented the awards to Deputies Adam Sandler, John Popp, Lee Martinez, and Ron
  Rhodes.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: announced that the Orange County Healthcare Agency has formed a
committee to study the feasibility of having private paramedics support the Orange County Fire
Authority. The pilot program study has shown very favorable results and he noted that he
strongly endorses all efforts to improve paramedic services.

Dennis Lumley, M.V.: asked if the Elks Lodge bingo games can be advertised on the community
message board at the corner of La Paz and Marguerite and he suggested that all messages should
appear for a shorter amount of time so they will display more frequently.

Helen Workun, M.V.: stated that hundreds of people had a great time attending the Arts Alive
festival at Oso Viejo Park last weekend. Ms. Workun thanked the City of Mission Viejo for
hosting the special event and being such a faithful supporter of the arts, city staff for their
collective, creative talents and all of the volunteers who worked so hard that day.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 5, and 16 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  3  May 6, 2013
   Approved the Minutes for regular City Council Meeting of April 15, 2013, as presented.

4.  Check Register Dated April 12, 2013 in the Amount of $282,935.35

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Landscape and Irrigation Materials and Supplies

  (1) Approved Fourth Amendment to the existing contract with John Deere Landscape, Inc.
  for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not to exceed $540,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to
  John Deere Landscape, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an
  amount not to exceed $270,000.00, pending adoption of the 2013-2015 budget by the City
  Council.

7.  Annual Routine Landscape Rodent Pest Control Contract â?? Contract Area 1

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with Animal Pest Management
  Services, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract
  amount by an amount not to exceed $70,613.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase
  order to Animal Pest Management Services, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June
  30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed $ 35,307.00, pending adoption of the 2013-2015
  budget by the City Council.

8.  Annual Routine Landscape Rodent Pest Control Contract - Contract Area 2

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with Animal Pest Management
  Services, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013 through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract
  amount by an amount not to exceed $31,087.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase
  order to Animal Pest Management Services, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June
  30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed $15,544.00, pending adoption of the 2013-2015
  budget by the City Council.

9.  Annual Technical Irrigation Contract

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with A.C. Landscape, Inc. for the
  period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract amount by an amount
  not to exceed $474,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to A.C.
  Landscape, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, in an amount not to
  exceed $237,000.00.

10. Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting, and Sealing Services Contract

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Bonanza Steam
  Cleaning, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, to increase the contract
  amount by an amount not to exceed $94,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase

City Council Minutes  4  May 6, 2013
   order to Bonanza Steam Cleaning, Inc. for the period July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014,
  in an amount not to exceed $47,000.00.

11. Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services at Various Park Sites and Facilities

  (1) Approved the Fourth Amendment for the Annual Routine Janitorial and Related
  Services at Various Park Sites and Facilities contract to Vocational Visions for the period
  of July 1, 2013, to June 30, 2015, in an amount not to exceed $242,776.00; and (2)
  authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Vocational Visions for the period of July 1,
  2013, through June 30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed $121,388.00, pending adoption of
  the 2013-15 budget by the City Council.

12. Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

  Adopted Resolution 13-27 Approving the Proposed Trash Rate Adjustments for
  Residential (1.98% Increase From $12.40 to $12.65 per Month), Commercial (1.99%
  Increase), and Roll-Off (2.04% Increase) Services Effective July 1, 2013.

13. 2011 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

14. City of Mission Viejo Amended Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement
  Program Beginning with the 2012-13 Fiscal Year

  (1) Adopted Resolution 13-28 Amending a Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement
  Program, Beginning with the 2012-13 Fiscal Year, to Include New Projects and
  Adjustments to Existing Projects that have been Awarded Grant Funding Through the
  OCTA Renewed Measure M2 Environmental Cleanup Program (ECP), the OCTA
  Renewed Measure M2 Regional Traffic Synchronization Program (TSP), and the Caltrans
  Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP), in Accordance with Renewed Measure M2
  Reporting Requirements; and (2) directed the Director of Public Works to transmit the
  amended Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program Beginning with the
  2012-13 Fiscal Year to the Orange County Transportation Authority by June 30, 2013.

15. 2012 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the

City Council Minutes  5  May 6, 2013
   faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

17. 2013 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Overlay (CIP 838)

  Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the subject project.

18. Purchase of Janitorial-Related Paper, Plastic and Chemical Supplies for City Building
  Facilities

  Approved Second Amendment to the existing contract to Waxie Sanitary Supply in the
  amount of $23,000 for FY 2012-2013.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

19. Mission Viejo Dog Park (CIP 313)

  Robert Setareh and Farro Koochek, Pima Corporation, Los Angeles: expressed
  disappointment that the City is considering re-bidding the project. Mr. Setareh stated that
  they look forward to submitting another bid and hope that Pima will be successful next
  time. He also discussed Pima's work history and offered to answer the Council's questions.

  The City Council Members asked questions of the Pima representatives and expressed
  concern that Pima did not provide five reliable and expert references.

  The following presented a written comment in opposition to the dog park: Harry Lenczyk.
  M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to reject
  all bids and authorize staff to advertise and rebid the project for the dog park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to amend the
  motion and cancel this dog park location, erect a fence around an existing park and save the
  City $1.5 million.

City Council Minutes  6  May 6, 2013
   On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 13-29 Approving the Property Tax Exchange Agreement Between the City of
  Mission Viejo and the County of Orange Regarding the Arroyo Trabuco Open Space and
  the Mission Viejo Dog Park Property Line Reorganization.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S COMMISSION

21. Youth Services Contract for FY 2013-2014 and FY 2014-2015 with the Saddleback
  Valley Unified School District Department of Recreation and Community Services.

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve
  the Community Services Commission's recommendation for (1) approval of the Youth
  Services Contract amendment with the Saddleback Valley Unified School District
  (SVUSD) Department of Recreation and Community Services in the amount of $725,000
  for FY 2013-14 and $731,000 for FY 2014-15; (2) approval for implementing a $25
  registration fee for each semester (fall and spring) during the school year, and $40
  registration fee for the summer program for the Kid's Factory program; and (3) defer
  approving a Middle School/Junior High fitness program until the 2013-15 budget
  deliberations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

22. Renewal of Rental Contract with Outta Bounds Events for Use of the Thomas R.
  Potocki Conference Center for Fiscal Years 2013-2015

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  7  May 6, 2013
   Scott Ramirez, Outta Bounds: responding to a Council question on attendance, he stated
  that an estimated 150-200 children attend Outta Bounds between the school year program
  and spring break and summer camps.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
  Community Services Commission's recommendation that the current Rental Contract with
  Outta Bounds Events for Use of the Thomas R. Potocki Conference Center be extended for
  Fiscal Years 2013-2015 in the amount of $6,000 annually with the understanding that if
  another group is interested in using the Potocki Center, the City has the flexibility and the
  right to consider other programs for the facility and to run those through the Community
  Services Commission assessment process.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

20. Amendment to Indenture of Trust and other documents related to the Mission Viejo
  Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Variable Rate Demand
  Revenue Bonds (Mission Viejo Mall Improvement Project), 1999 Series A

  Council Member Ury informed the Mayor that he had to leave for the airport to catch a
  flight and he departed the meeting at 8:01 p.m.

  Special Counsel Celeste Brady, Stradling, Yocca Carlson and Rauth, presented the staff
  report.

  David Brodsly, Managing Director, KNN Public Finance, answered the City Council's
  questions regarding Union Bank's position as the re-marketing agent in the proposed
  transaction.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to adopt
  MVCDFA Resolution 13-01 Electing to Substitute the Remarketing Agent, Approving the
  Form and Authorizing Execution of a Remarketing Agent Agreement with the Successor
  Remarketing Agent, Electing to Remove the Confirming Letter of Credit, Approving the
  Form and Authorizing Execution of Amendments to the Indenture of Trust, Dated as of
  May 1, 1999, as Amended, Approving Amendments to the Reimbursement Agreement,
  Dated as of May 1, 1999, and Approving a Fee Letter, all Relating to the $31,100,000
  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority Variable Rate Demand
  Revenue Bonds (Mission Viejo Mall Improvement Project), 1999 Series A (Tax-Exempt)
  and Approving Official Actions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  8  May 6, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

RECESS

At the hour of 8:10 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:25
p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent.)

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated April 5, 2013 in the Amount of $1,659,720.29

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment to Tomark Sports for $29,000 and
  stated that combined with a $17,000 payment to Southern Hemisphere Shade, the City
  spent almost $47,500 to rehab a sports park.

  City Manger Wilberg indicated that staff will look into these expenditures and get back to
  the Council with details.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

5.  Check Register dated April 19, 2013 in the amount of $2,107,362.90

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to Bravo Sign and Designs.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that there were
  monies remaining from a State grant for the wayfinding and kiosk program. This
  expenditure was for 10 trail signs and some additional replacement signage for future
  needs.

  Council Member Schlicht also inquired about cell site payments to LD Acquisition
  Company 9 LLC.

  City Attorney Bill Curley responded that ATS Communications has sold all of its cell site
  interests as permitted under their agreement with the City. City Manager Wilberg noted that
  staff will let the Council know if LD Acquisition Company 9 LLC is the company that
  purchased ATS' interests.

City Council Minutes  9  May 6, 2013
   Council Member Schlicht asked if anyone on staff is looking at radiation from cell sites.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that he is not aware of anyone doing that but he will
  verify with staff tomorrow.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

16. Eighth Amendment to City Manager Employment Agreement

  City Council Member Schlicht announced that she disagrees with the statement in the staff
  report that the City Manager's contract has been thoroughly reviewed by the City Council.
  She noted that she still opposes a pay raise without an accountability clause in the contract
  and she was not particularly enthralled with the way the review went.

  Council Member Leckness noted that it has been 6 years since the City Manager has had a
  pay raise and in fact, over the years, he has turned proposed pay raises down.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley expressed her appreciation for the City Manager and stated that he
  is well respected up and down the state. Mr. Wilberg has seen the City through some very
  difficult times and under his leadership, the City has continued to thrive. Not only has he
  not had a pay raise over the past 6 years but he will be contributing the money back to his
  pension contribution.

  Mayor Reardon agreed with Mayor Pro Tem Kelley's comments and noted that the Council
  actually offered him more but Mr. Wilberg wanted his salary increase to reflect what the
  employees are doing to pay back to their retirement.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  approve the Eighth Amendment to the City Manager Employment Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Ury

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

23. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

City Council Minutes  10  May 6, 2013
   Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that OCERS Board recently granted OCFA's request to
  postpone a vote on the issue of amortizing the OCER's unfunded liability, however OCFA
  has still not provided a requested report on the OCFA's own unfunded liability. Mr.
  Wontrobski further discussed the hazmat inspection fees investigation which has been
  undertaken by the Orange County DA and he noted that OCFA has still not answered his
  question as to whether or not OCFA is conducting its own best practice audit on the hazmat
  fees matter.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

24. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern
  TCA and she will have a report at the next meeting.

25. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin
  Hills TCA and she will have a report at the next meeting.

27. CUSD Ad Hoc Committee Report

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to send a letter to the CUSD Board
  supporting CUSD staff's recommendation to end the CFD 87-1 Mello Roos taxes at the end
  of the bond indebtedness period in 2020.

28. Orange County Vector Control District

  Council Member Leckness presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

29. Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

City Manager Wilberg announced that the League of California Cities will hold a webinar on
May 16, 2013, at 10:00 a.m. regarding some of the proposed policy changes at CalPERS. He
invited the Council Members to stop by City Hall to watch the webinar if they are interested. Mr.
Wilberg also reminded the Council that he will be out of town on May 20 so he will not attend
the next City Council Meeting.

City Attorney’s Report

City Council Minutes  11  May 6, 2013
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

30. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness announced that he enjoyed the MADD presentation earlier in the
evening to honor the deputies who have made 25 or more DUI arrests. He also discussed his
attendance at the Rotary Club's Prayer Breakfast and it was a very nice event with a great
turnout. Council Member Leckness asked if the Council can review the street sweeping RFP at
the next Council Meeting.

By consensus, the City Council directed staff to return with an agenda item at the next meeting
for review of the street sweeping RFP.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht asked for Council consensus to have staff provide a list of events and
the cost associated with each.

Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas announced that staff is still working on a listing
of special events and the numbers have not been finalized.

Council Member Schlicht further asked about programs and classes that the City is funding at the
various locations. City Manager Wilberg noted that staff has been focusing on the special events
and will bring a draft of that document to the Council Meeting on May 20.

Council Member Schlicht wished resident Joe Holtzman a happy birthday. She announced that
she has been invited by the Saddleback Republican Assembly to discuss city issues at the SRA
meeting on Thursday, May 16, 2013, at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. Council
Member Schlicht discussed her attendance at recent events including the Arts Alive festival and
the National Day of Prayer event at the civic center. She concluded her comments with a quote
from Thomas Paine: "Beware of the greedy hand of government thrusting itself into every corner
and crevice of industry."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury was absent.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she was helping her daughter with a move and she was
sorry to miss the last Council Meeting. She outlined her attendance at the Rotary Prayer

City Council Minutes  12  May 6, 2013
 Breakfast and a Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) General Assembly.
She noted that she will give a report on the SCAG meeting at the next City Council meeting. She
also discussed her attendance at other recent events including the Marine Day at the Lake, the
3rd Grade Environmental Fair, Arts Alive, and a Vocational Visions fundraising dinner. Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley reminded residents that the Community of Character word for the month of May
is moral courage and the character movie is Mulan which will be shown in the Council Chamber
on Sunday, May 19, 2013.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon highlighted two events that she attended last week; the National Day of Prayer
and the Rotary Prayer Breakfast. She also reiterated Mayor Pro Tem Kelley's comments on the
Arts Alive festival and she thanked staff and the many volunteers who accomplish so much with
the City's events. Mayor Reardon discussed the prescription drug abuse epidemic and stated that
it has become a public safety issue. She announced that more than 100 residents took advantage
of the National Take Back Day event on April 27 where over 347 pounds of unused or expired
medication were disposed-of safely. She noted that the prescription drug problem is even evident
as real estate agents are telling their clients to remove prescription drugs from medicine cabinets
when they hold an open house. Mayor Reardon announced two upcoming events for residents on
the subject of prescription drug abuse. On Wednesday, May 8, 2013, from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. in
the Council Chamber, the City will host a presentation meant to educate adults and parents on
the epidemic. Also, on Wednesday, May 15 from 7:30 to 9:00 p.m., there will be another
program for adults and teens on prescription drug abuse. Mayor Reardon highlighted a very
complimentary comment card that she received from a resident who loves the library and noted
that it is hard to get her kids to leave. She also announced that the library is hosting a new Baby
Lap-Sit Early Literacy Class, a program for parents and their babies ages 6-18 months. The
classes are held on Tuesdays at 10:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. in the newly remodeled Storytime
Room. Mayor Reardon concluded her comments by discussing volunteerism and she highlighted
several special individuals including Michael Munguia, a double amputee who volunteered at the
Earth Day event, SCAT volunteer Cliff McKinley who has donated 8,338 hours of service to the
community, and City employee and artist Kevin Peterson who created a chalk drawing at Arts
Alive, winning an award for the best artwork for the theme.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:02 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in memory of Tricia Scott to Monday, May 20,
2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 20, 2013

City Council Minutes  13  May 6, 2013
